s1.syndrome_frame: a growing, painless breast nodule with calcifications
salient_findings: growing, painless nodule in the left breast
hypoechoic, poorly circumscribed nodule on ultrasonography
key_facts: 2-year history of a growing breast nodule
nodule located in the lower outer quadrant of the left breast
lesion is firm and mobile
lesion is well defined
no skin changes
no nipple discharge
no palpable lymphadenopathy
mammography shows a well-defined mass with multiple pleomorphic calcifications
ultrasonography reveals a hypoechoic, subcutaneous nodule
marked posterior acoustic shadowing from microcalcifications
no locoregional lymphadenopathy
lesion classified as ACR BI-RADS IV

shortlist.label: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with growing nodule and pleomorphic calcifications

shortlist.label: Ductal Carcinoma In Situ
shortlist.why_kept: presence of calcifications and well-defined mass, possible precursor to invasive cancer

shortlist.label: Fibroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: common benign breast tumor, can present as a firm and mobile nodule

shortlist.label: Phyllodes Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: rare tumor that can grow rapidly, may have similar imaging characteristics

shortlist.label: Papillary Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: less common type of breast cancer, can present with calcifications and a well-defined mass

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple pleomorphic calcifications on mammography and a hypoechoic nodule with marked posterior acoustic shadowing from microcalcifications on ultrasonography are characteristic of Ductal Carcinoma In Situ, which is often associated with microcalcifications and has a more benign appearance compared to invasive carcinomas.

rejected.label: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma
rejected.why: Invasive Ductal Carcinoma typically presents with more aggressive features such as irregular margins, spiculations, and lymphadenopathy, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Fibroadenoma
rejected.why: Fibroadenomas are usually well-circumscribed, mobile, and without microcalcifications, which does not match the ultrasonography and mammography findings of this case.

rejected.label: Phyllodes Tumor
rejected.why: Phyllodes Tumors are typically large, rapidly growing masses that can be either benign or malignant, but they do not typically present with the microcalcifications seen in this case.

rejected.label: Papillary Carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary Carcinoma often presents as a solid, hypoechoic mass with internal vascularity on ultrasonography, and while it can have calcifications, the presence of pleomorphic calcifications and the specific ultrasonographic features in this case are more suggestive of Ductal Carcinoma In Situ.
